texts.preamble: Awadhesh @ Kallu Sharma vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 20 May, 2024 Author: Sunita Yadav Bench: Sunita Yadav 1 In The High Court Of Madhya Pradesh At Gwalior Before Hon'Ble Smt. Justice Sunita Yadav
texts.facts: This is first application filed by the applicant under Section 438 of the Cr.P.C. for grant of anticipatory bail relating to FIR No.306 of 2023 registered at Police Station Gohad Chauraha, District Bhind (M.P.) for the offence under Sections 420, 272 & 273 of IPC. Allegations against the applicant / accused, in short, are that on 03/11/2023 Food Safety Officer Avinash Gupta alongwith other officials made an inspection at Kamini Sales Agency Gohad Chauraha where applicant was found to be selling the materials which are used for preparation of adulterated milk. In presence of independent witnesses, seven samples of adulterated substance were taken, shop was sealed and seizure memo was prepared under the Food Safety Act, 2006 and sent to the concerned Laboratory for testing. On the basis of aforesaid, a case was registered against the applicant.
texts.arguments: Learned counsel for the applicant argued that applicant is innocent and has been falsely implicated. It is further argued that no substance of food material was found in the applicant's shop and only on the basis of the allegation that the applicant was selling the equipment related to dairy product, present FIR has been registered which is prima-facie illegal, contrary and against the law. Further argument is that if the sample found to be unsafe then prior making the prosecution, the sanction is required from the Commissioner u/S. 42(3) of The Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 but in the present case no sanction has been obtained from the Commissioner. It is further argued that in case sample is found to be sub-standard and adulterated then prosecution cannot initiate any criminal action because u/Ss. 51 & 57 of The Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 only penalty can be imposed and no imprisonment is provided under such offences. In support of his submissions, counsel for the applicant relied upon the decisions of Apex Court in the case of Ram Nath Vs. The State of U.P. passed in Cr.A. No.472 of 2012 decided on 21/02/2024 and in the case of Sushil Kumar Gupta Vs. State of West Bengal arising out of SLP (Crl.) No.15495 of 2023 decided on 22.03.2024. It is further argued that the applicant is permanent resident of District Bhind (M.P.) and there is no possibility of his absconding or tampering with the prosecution evidence. Under these circumstances, he prays for grant of anticipatory bail to the applicant. O n the other hand, learned State counsel vehemently opposed the application and prayed for its rejection.
